subject.title: Synchronous transcript I/O scales with tool-result payload size and can block the event loop the liveness monitor samples

question: Should this issue require current-main live measurement before an async SessionManager persistence refactor is sponsored, or is the source-backed synchronous hot path enough to approve design work now?
rationale: The source path is real, but the default cap changes the reporter's repro shape and the fix would touch a broad session-state boundary that automation should not redesign without owner intent.

options.title: Require measurement first
options.body: Keep this open with maintainer review until a current-main large-payload run shows eventLoopDelayMaxMs correlation and any abort/recovery outcome under the active SessionManager path.

options.title: Sponsor async design now
options.body: A maintainer can accept the source-backed risk and direct an owner-led refactor of active SessionManager persistence without waiting for live reproduction.

options.title: Narrow to cap-only mitigation
options.body: Treat the remaining risk as sufficiently reduced by tool-result caps and only revisit if new logs show configured or uncapped payloads still causing stalls.

recommendation.title: Require measurement first
recommendation.body: Keep this open with maintainer review until a current-main large-payload run shows eventLoopDelayMaxMs correlation and any abort/recovery outcome under the active SessionManager path.

likelyOwner.reason: The transcript writer seam work makes this the best available owner boundary for deciding whether and how to move active persistence off the synchronous SessionManager API.
